subject: Files
notes: SHARING WITH NO OTHER, all four sentences. (a) 'specifies exclusive access to a physical file' + 'Associating this file connector with the physical file will be unsuccessful if the physical file is currently open through other file connectors' + 'subsequent requests to open the physical file through other file connectors before this file connector is closed will be unsuccessful' -- INSIDE the run unit this is Table 19's NoOtherAnyMode ROW and COLUMN, both Unsuccessful in all five/seven cells (kb/Work PB321, OpenTable19.cs#Cell; unit:OpenTable19Tests.NineOneFifteenRules_ReproduceTheWholeTable derives the whole table from these three rules and matches it cell for cell). Golden leg L2 of pb740_clauseless_share is the corpus witness: OPEN INPUT on the NO OTHER connector = '00', a second OPEN INPUT = '61' (9.1.13.9 1) a)). (b) OUTSIDE it -- 9.1.15, 'The successful opening of a file establishes a file lock for the applicable sharing rules, thereby preventing other run units from opening that file with incompatible sharing rules' -- the OS share mode IS that lock, and FileLockPosture.OfSharingMode maps NO OTHER to FileShare.None. That half was INVERTED until kb/Work PB740: a NO OTHER connector was a 'sharing participant' and participants opened FileShare.ReadWrite, so an external process appended four bytes to a file the program held open (measured cross-process, drive.py), while a connector with no clause at all refused the same write. unit:FileLockPostureDriftTests.TheFileLockIsTheSharingMode_MeasuredFromOutsideTheConnector measures all three modes from a handle outside the connector, with the clause-less and ALL OTHER arms as controls -- a share mode names no requester, so a handle the test opens is exactly as foreign as another program's. (c) 'Record locks are ignored' -- FileRegistry.LocksEffective returns false for a connector open in the no-other mode, measured by unit:FileLockPostureDriftTests.TheSharingModeAlsoDecidesWhetherRecordLocksAreInEffect against the in-effect arms of rules 2) and 3). COBOL-85 has no SHARING clause and no 9.1.15, so the rule's antecedent cannot arise there. ⛔ THE KEYED HALF IS NOW CLOSED (kb/Work PB771), so the scope note this row carried is replaced rather than kept. §9.1.15 3) names no organization and §9.1.6 says there are three, so all three owe the file lock; RELATIVE and INDEXED held no long-lived host handle at all between OPEN and CLOSE and therefore established none. MEASURED before the fix, on this tree: with a SHARING WITH NO OTHER connector holding an INDEXED (and again a RELATIVE) file open I-O, another run unit's 4-byte append SUCCEEDED, and the CLOSE then rewrote the file from the OPEN's snapshot (46->50->46 bytes indexed, 28->32->28 relative) with '00' reported on both sides. KeyedConnector.TakeFileLock now takes the connector's own HostFile.OpenConnectorStream handle on every OpenCore arm that has a physical file, carrying the posture FileLockPosture derived; RecordFraming.ReadStore/WriteStore take that STREAM rather than a path, so the store's load and persist travel through the lock instead of around it (a second handle would ask for access the connector's own FileShare.None forbids -- kb/Work PB713); ReleaseFileLock gives it back at the CLOSE and at an unsuccessful OPEN (FileConnector.AbandonOpen), and KeyedConnector.Reposture rebuilds it when the admitted set changes. unit:FileLockPostureDriftTests.EveryOrganizationHoldsALiveFileLockWhileOpen measures the lock from a handle OUTSIDE the connector for every (organization x open mode) and measures the give-back at the CLOSE; the same class's TheFileLockIsTheSharingMode_MeasuredFromOutsideTheConnector and TheHostHandleNeverVetoesWhatTable19Permits now carry the organization axis too (4 of 9 arms, and 24 cells of the matrix, were RED on the pre-fix tree). conformance:cases/9.1.15-Sharing-mode/pb771_keyed_file_lock_2023 and its 2002 twin certify the half a COBOL program can observe: the gate INSIDE the run unit is still the file connectors and Table 19, for both keyed organizations, which a new handle could silently have broken. retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/FileRegistry.cs#Conflicts (FileRegistry.Conflicts and SyncHostPostures were deleted (kb/Work PB322): the file lock is the sharing mode's own posture handed down in SharedOpenAttempt, and arbitration is Table19.Conflicts) retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Runtime/IO/FileRegistry.cs#SyncHostPostures (FileRegistry.Conflicts and SyncHostPostures were deleted (kb/Work PB322): the file lock is the sharing mode's own posture handed down in SharedOpenAttempt, and arbitration is Table19.Conflicts)
